q: Pictured: crushed stone. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Eskondro / Escondro” is the vernacular for crushed stone. Likely a variant of Spanish escombro “rubble”; crushed stone is broken rubble.

q: Pictured: ceiling. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Kisame” is the vernacular for ceiling. Clipped from Spanish zaquizamí, which came from Arabic for “roof in the sky” (per Wiktionary). Memory hook: the ceiling is the sky of the room; pair it with sahig (floor).

q: Pictured: wainscoting tile. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Asolehos / Asolejo” is the vernacular for wainscoting tile. Origin: Spanish azulejo “glazed tile”, from Arabic az-zulayj. Asolejo sounds like azulejo.

q: Pictured: cement tile. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Baldosa” is the vernacular for cement tile. Origin: Spanish baldosa “floor tile”.

q: Pictured: mortar joint. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Kostura / Kustura” is the vernacular for mortar joint. Origin: Spanish costura “seam, stitching”. A mortar joint is the seam that stitches the bricks together.

q: Pictured: plaster (stucco). Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Palitada” is the vernacular for plaster (stucco). Origin: Spanish paletada “a trowelful”, from paleta “trowel”. Plaster is applied with a trowel.

q: Pictured: partition. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Dingding” is the vernacular for partition. Origin: native Tagalog dingding “wall”. A partition is a thin wall.

q: Pictured: concrete slab. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Larga Masa” is the vernacular for concrete slab. Origin: Spanish larga “long, large” + masa “mass, mix, dough”: a large mass of concrete mix.

q: Pictured: wood grain. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Haspe” is the vernacular for wood grain. Likely from Spanish jaspe “jasper”; jaspeado means streaked or veined, like wood grain.

q: Pictured: cement brick. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Ladrilyo / Landrilyo” is the vernacular for cement brick. Origin: Spanish ladrillo “brick”, with an extra n in the Filipino form.

q: Pictured: masonry fill. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Lastilyas” is the vernacular for masonry fill. Likely borrowed from Spanish lastre “ballast, gravel fill” with a diminutive ending: the gravelly fill.

q: Pictured: varnish. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Monyeka” is the vernacular for varnish. Likely from Spanish muñeca “doll”, which also names the rag pad used to rub on varnish.

q: Pictured: putty. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Masilya” is the vernacular for putty. Origin: Spanish masilla “putty”, from masa “dough, paste”.

q: Pictured: earth fill. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Eskumbro / Escombro” is the vernacular for earth fill. Origin: Spanish escombro “rubble, debris”.

q: Pictured: floorboards. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Dotal” is the vernacular for floorboards. Origin not confirmed and not obviously Spanish. Memory hook: dotal ~ “dots”: the rows of nail dots across a floor of boards.
